requirements.requirement: Seed-starting tray of at least four cells
requirements.evidence: Four full bases in a row (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:-1,1,0;full) each holding a bin, visible from above with seedlings prop:1-4

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a draining bin
requirements.evidence: Each of the 4 cells has bin stem hex-bin-full-drain (bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0, bin:0,1,0, bin:-1,1,0 ~hex-bin-full-drain)

requirements.requirement: Suitable for seed starting (soil + seedlings shown)
requirements.evidence: All four bins filled with soil and planted via fill_and_plant: basil, mint, parsley, chives seedlings; check_build ok, meshClash clear, no prop warnings

finish.summary: Built a 4-cell seed-starting tray: four joined full hex bases in a row, each with a full-depth drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain), soil-filled and planted with basil, mint, parsley and chives seedlings. Open faces capped and joints locked; check_build passes with meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Seed tray, four-plus draining cells — I'll lay out four bins on a hex base and check what's available.
